TRADE: Each month, across up to 55 liquid futures/forward instruments spanning commodities, equity indexes, government bonds, and currencies, take a volatility-scaled long position in every instrument whose trailing 12-month excess return is positive and a volatility-scaled short position in every instrument whose trailing 12-month excess return is negative (each leg sized to a constant 40% ex-ante annualized volatility via a one-month-lagged EWMA estimator); equal-weight the positions across all available instruments each month into a single diversified time-series momentum (TSMOM) factor, rebalanced monthly.
PRIMARY RESULT: Over January 1985-December 2009 (300 months), the replicated diversified TSMOM factor has an annualized Sharpe ratio of 1.25, total return 4046.6%, max drawdown -20.6%, and FF5 alpha 15.93%/year (t = 6.02), matching the paper's description of '12% per year' volatility and 'a Sharpe ratio greater than one ... roughly 2.5 times the Sharpe ratio for the equity market portfolio.' Controlling for MKT/SMB/HML/UMD, the monthly alpha is 1.198% (t = 5.855, R2 = 0.116) versus the paper's 1.58% (t = 7.99, R2 = 0.14), with UMD loading 0.229 (t = 5.394) versus the paper's 0.28 (t = 6.78).
REASSURANCE:
- An independent engine rebuild from raw daily futures data matches the replicator's own strategy series exactly (max |delta| = 0.0), including an SP500 sub-panel matching over 326 months.
- The horizon signature replicates: continuation through k<=12 months decays to weak reversal by k=24-48.
- TSMOM subsumes cross-sectional momentum in aggregate: XSMOM-ALL on TSMOM gives beta 0.72 (t 16.28), R2 47% versus paper 0.66 (t 15.17), 44%.
- The straddle-like payoff is present: TSMOM +10.2% in 2008Q4 while S&P 500 futures fell -23.0%.
CAVEATS:
- Several inputs are data-forced substitutes (US T-bill rate for all instruments, EW-futures proxies for MSCI/Barclays/GSCI, currency futures instead of forwards, unscaled bond duration); these affect secondary tables more than the headline factor.

- The sample covers only 9 of the paper's 21 formation years and 41% of its firm-years; the abstract's full-period 23% figure is unreachable by construction here.
